waves.name: Setup and utility jobs
waves.rationale: Seven jobs that run no application program and touch no dataset another entry point uses. They prove the toolchain and the job runner on the lowest-risk work. Several are one-time setup (DEFCUST, ESDSRRDS) and may be retired rather than ported, which only telemetry can settle.
waves.unblocks: The job runner and the JCL-to-new-platform conversion that every later batch wave uses.

waves.name: Read-only batch dumps and the import program
waves.rationale: Batch programs that read the masters and write nothing another entry point uses. This is the first wave that exercises the record layouts, so it is where the behavioral-equivalence harness is built and proven on read paths before any write path moves.
waves.unblocks: The layout copybooks and the output-comparison harness that waves 5 to 7 reuse. It also gives the client a read-side check of the ported master files.

waves.name: Sign-on, menus and read-only screens
waves.rationale: Online programs that write nothing another entry point uses. Sign-on and the two menus are one strongly connected component and move whole. COTRN00C and COTRN01C are a second component and are flagged god modules, so they go behind a facade. All of the computed calls here were read and resolve to literal program names or a literal menu table, so the wave is bounded, but confidence stays below high.
waves.unblocks: The navigation layer. Every online writer in wave 7 returns to these menus through the shared COMMAREA, so the routing convention is fixed here.

waves.name: Build, compile and GDG definition jobs
waves.rationale: Jobs and procs that touch shared datasets only through a utility. Most are build and compile steps that the new platform replaces with its own pipeline, so this wave is mostly retirement. It is a chore wave that delivers nothing a business stakeholder names, and it is kept because the extractor placed each unit by fact. DEFGDGD defines generation datasets that the report path in wave 6 writes to, so it must exist before wave 6.
waves.unblocks: The generation-dataset definitions that the transaction report and backup jobs in wave 6 need.

waves.name: Reference-data refresh and statements
waves.rationale: Batch writers that share no program or output dataset with any other group: the customer, cross-reference, discount-group, category and type refreshes, the statement run, the export, and the CICS close and open bracket. One argument covers them: each reloads a reference file from a flat file. The close and open jobs must move with the first job that depends on them.
waves.unblocks: The close and open bracket that wave 6 depends on, and the export format that the import in wave 2 reads back.

waves.name: Master refresh, daily posting and transaction report
waves.rationale: All three must-not-break items live here. Posting (CBTRN02C) writes the transaction, account and category-balance masters, the refresh jobs rebuild the same masters, and the report reads them, so they share datasets and the shell wrappers order them. They move as one coupled group. It is a large wave but one sentence describes it: batch jobs that write the masters. The order inside the wave comes from the wrappers, not from dependencies, and is weaker than it looks. CORPT00C submits the report by embedded JCL, so the online report path moves here too. The wave cannot ship until the VSAM masters sit behind a facade that wave 7's online writers also use. Confidence is low: this is the highest-blast wave, the extractor reads no SORT cards or assembler, and the wrapper order is unverified.
waves.unblocks: Wave 7, which cannot move its screens until the masters are behind the facade built here. It is also the wave a steering committee can name: the nightly cycle runs on the new platform.

waves.name: Online screens that update the masters
waves.rationale: Online programs that write the account, card, transaction and user files that the batch cycle also uses. They go after the batch writers because the facade over the masters is built in wave 6, and they cannot go before it. COACTUPC is the largest program in the system at 3,368 lines and is the heaviest single port. Every program here makes a computed call, all resolved to literal targets.
waves.unblocks: Retiring the old CICS file definitions, since nothing online reads them directly after this wave.

waves.name: Authorization and transaction-type unload and load
waves.rationale: The IMS, DB2 and MQ optional modules that touch no dataset shared with another group. None sits on a must-not-break path. IMS DBD and PSB, DB2 DDL and DCLGEN files were not read by the extractor, so the real data model of this wave is unseen.
waves.unblocks: Wave 9. It also removes the IMS and MQ runtimes from the estate.

waves.name: Authorization screens and transaction-type maintenance
waves.rationale: DB2 and IMS programs coupled through the transaction-type table and the authorization database. COPAUS0C and COPAUS1C are one strongly connected component and COPAUS0C is a god module, so it moves behind a facade. This is the last wave because it is outside the three must-not-break items and depends on unparsed IMS and DB2 definitions.
waves.unblocks: Nothing. It is the tail of the plan, and it can be deferred or dropped if the client retires the optional modules.

unassigned.reason: Not reached by any static edge. The cartographer read all 28 computed calls and none can reach it, but an operator or external scheduler outside the tree could run it, so it stays unplaced and unknown (app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:1).

deviations.reason: Must-not-break item: the account and card master refresh is one operation, run as ACCTFILE then CARDFILE by the same wrapper. The seed split it across waves 5 and 6. A boundary that cuts one refresh in two cannot be tested as one, so CARDFILE joins ACCTFILE.
